document.title: Bad News on Pak Afghan Policy: GOP Support for the Taliban Appears to be Getting Stronger
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Taliban File Update
document.note: [Confidential] Sourced to journalist Ahmed Rashid and UN adviser Arnie Schifferdecker, shows Pakistan agreed to give the Taliban 300 million rupees (about $6.5 million), at 50 million rupees monthly, to pay Taliban officials and commanders. Pakistani Afghan desk officer Ayyaz Wazir called it humanitarian assistance. Comment discusses the effect of the May 1998 nuclear tests and India-Pakistan tension.

sources_cited: Conversations with Ahmed Rashid and Arnie Schifferdecker
key_claims: Embassy assessed that GOP support for the Taliban was getting stronger after the May 1998 nuclear tests.
The GOP reportedly decided to give the Taliban 300 million rupees over six months to pay salaries of officials and commanders.
MFA and ISID officials, previously feigning support for a broad-based government, now openly backed the Taliban.
Rashid speculated ISID was using the Taliban as a bargaining chip with the West.
Schifferdecker suggested ISID was exploiting Prime Minister Sharif's preoccupation to push its pro-Taliban line.
